question: Does past GT point motion improve actual action prediction when delivered immediately before the ACT action head?
primary_comparison: late tracks minus late current geometry; negative MSE difference favors past motion
primary_metric: full 100-offset actual joint-target MSE, valid scalar entries weighted, rad^2, prior latent zero
secondary_metrics: 64 predeclared evenly spaced training windows evaluated with prior zero

conditions.late_geometry: RGB history + current joints + current point geometry; past point values/validity masked
conditions.late_tracks: same inputs and capacity plus observed past GT tracks

late_interface: same existing trajectory MLP, remove point tokens from encoder, cross-attend decoder features to point tokens immediately before the action linear layer; fixed residual scale 0.1; 8 heads; attention dropout zero
statistics: report all paired seed deltas and episode breakdowns; do not treat overlapping windows as independent; no winner selection using secondary strata
early_baselines: audit and diagnose existing checkpoints; old 2000-step training used B20Z and therefore early/late interaction remains exploratory until same-hardware reruns; late tracks versus late geometry is hardware paired
compute: shared development H800 GPUs only, one 8GiB process budget per selected GPU, at least 12GiB free before start; no whole-node allocation; never affect colleagues' jobs
decision: If late tracks do not consistently reduce full-chunk MSE, reject this particular late interface as sufficient evidence of motion benefit; do not conclude flow is intrinsically useless. Next isolate RGB-history redundancy or task motion dependence before more auxiliaries.
scope_limit: same garment, four repeatedly used development validation episodes; no independent generalization or closed-loop success claim; formal longer training remains held
